raw_response:
Forty-five years on this land, and I still think carefully each spring. Let me walk through what I'm planning.

I farm 12 mu total. I keep about 5 mu in cotton on my sandier western plot — it's drained well there, and cotton pays better per mu if the market holds. The other 7 mu I run wheat-maize double cropping. That's my food security and steady income. With just me and my wife at home now (the kids work in Handan), I manage most work myself but hire two people for cotton picking and wheat harvest.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October):** I put about 10 kg N/mu as base fertilizer last fall with diammonium phosphate — that gave me roughly 5 kg P too. Right now I'm planning spring topdressing: about 8 kg N/mu as urea at jointing, maybe mid-March. I'll irrigate at jointing and again at heading — two times at minimum, three if April stays dry. Expecting around 470 kg/mu if weather cooperates. Last year I got 490, but the year before a late frost cost me.

**Maize (going in after wheat harvest in mid-June):** Very tight window — maybe 5 days to clear straw and plant. I'll use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 type, from the agri-supply store. One compound base dose of about 8 kg N equivalent at planting, then topdress 10 kg N/mu at big trumpet stage. One irrigation at tasseling unless it rains well. I'm aiming for 520 kg/mu.

**Cotton:** Planting mid-April after the soil warms. I use an improved variety, about 40 yuan/mu for seed. I've cut back on N over the years — too much makes it grow lanky. About 12 kg N/mu split: half at planting, half at first flower. Phosphorus 6 kg/mu as base. Pesticide is the big cost — herbicide once pre-emergence, insecticide 3-4 times for bollworm and aphids. Irrigate twice if the season is dry. Expect 260 kg lint/mu.

Total cash I'll need upfront: about 5,800 yuan. I keep roughly 2,000 yuan in reserve because you never know — a pump breakdown, a pest outbreak, my wife's medicine.
